defects.description: EntryGateTests.test_project_state_records_r11_approved hardcoded latest_approved_round == 'V4-R11' as an R12 entry-gate precondition. PROJECT_STATE.json is a live pointer, not a historical log, so once R12 (and any later round) formally closed and advanced that field, the literal comparison broke by construction. This was caught at the R13 entry gate: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` reported 1288 total with 1 FAILURE instead of 1288 PASS.
defects.evidence: Test failure trace at R13 entry gate: AssertionError: 'V4-R12' != 'V4-R11' in test_project_state_records_r11_approved.
defects.resolution: Replaced the hardcoded literal with a round-ordinal comparison (latest_approved_round must be V4-R11 or a later round), preserving the original intent (R11 must be approved) without asserting an exact snapshot value that the next closed round would immediately invalidate. No production semantic changed; only a test assertion was corrected.

technical_debt.description: Every R7-R12 package repeats the same plain-dict-builder + sorted-key JSON-renderer pattern (build_*_contract/render_*_contract_json). No behavioral defect; a shared thin helper could reduce duplication in a dedicated post-V4 refactor.

V3-R9 readiness gate module mixes document parsing, evidence-closure computation, and file I/O in one large module (_execute performs the whole pipeline). Historical V3 code, unmodified by V4; safe to leave as-is per AGENTS.md ('do not silently change an approved upstream semantic contract').

Batch-request helper naming (`requests`, `request`) is generic across proposals/relations/classification services; harmless, but a future glossary of shared parameter-naming conventions could improve cross-package readability.
